page.layout: One printed page. Heading block at top (chapter number, argument summary, thesis title, question statement, section heading), then one column of running text with two marginal notes on the right. Catchword at lower right. Gathering signature at foot. The left edge of the facing page is not transcribed.

main_text.head: CAP. XVII.
Decimum nostrum Argumentum, ex parte Christi meritis, adversus Pontificiorum ultimum propugnaculum, seu potius latibulum defensionis suae: viz.
Christum meruisse nobis virtutem merendi vitam aeternam.
Quaestionis status de nostra virtute merendi ex Meritis Christi.
SECT. I.
main_text.p: PRotestantes ex Meritis Christi propriis opera nostra bona grata & accepta Deo reddi fideli-ter credunt, & palam constan-ter profitentur: Pontificii vero, propriis Meritis Christi diffisi, (ut statim patebit) suam peculiarem merendi virtutem, tanquam ex ejus Meritis sibi indultam, commini-scuntur. Adversarios ipsos audiamus aequam est. Lib. 2. de Justif. c. 10.{f} Stapletonus, Christus, inquit, nobis meruit virtutem merendi. A qua cantilena Lib. 5. de Justif. c. 17.{t} Bellarmi-nus didicit illam suam, Merita nostra innituntur [?]

page.notes: The first part of the first line is set in a large woodcut initial P, joined to "Rotestantes" as "PRotestantes". The marginal notes are keyed to the text marks f and t. "innituntur" is the most doubtful reading; the line is heavily worn and the word may read differently. The text breaks off at the foot of the column and continues on the next page. Catchword "Meritis" is at lower right. The top right corner carries faint show-through, which was ignored. The left edge of the facing page was excluded.
